cells.value: NDPA 2023 in force (assented 12 June 2023, per official Act text); NDPC operational and enforcing: GAID 2025 issued 20 March 2025 (signed by National Commissioner Olatunji); NDPC Annual Report 2025 records 146 investigations in 2025 (213 in 2024), 38,661 registered Data Controllers/Processors of Major Importance (2025; 36,052 in 2024), 306 licensed DPCOs, ~7,000 verified DPOs, and N4.99bn compliance revenue (2025).
cells.quality_evidence: GAID 2025 (117-pp directive with schedules, audit-fee tiers, complaint forms) operationalises the Act and replaces the NDPR 2019 regime; secondary legal analyses (Afriwise/Templars) give effect date 19 Sept 2025. NDPC has a Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan (SRAP) 2023-2027, statutory registration/audit machinery (services.ndpc.gov.ng), a codified restorative enforcement doctrine anchored in NDPA ss.46-48, and publishes annual reports (2023, 2024, 2025).
cells.scale_evidence: Enforcement is live and current: NDPC news 12 Aug 2026 announces investigations of UNILAG, Lotus Bank and Hackerbella Ltd; sector cumulative revenue tracked by NDPC rose from N5.5bn (2022) to N25.5bn (2025); registered DCPMI 38,661 and licensed DPCOs 306 (Annual Report 2025, published June 2026).
cells.source_title: NDPC Annual Report 2025 (Nigeria Data Protection Commission, June 2026)
cells.search_trail: ndpc.gov.ng homepage -> resources page (GAID 2025 PDF, NDPA 2023 PDF, Annual Reports 2023/2024/2025 deep links) -> Annual Report 2025 full text (investigation/enforcement section pp.22-23, statistics p.27) -> GAID 2025 full text (issuance clause, 20 March 2025) -> NDPA 2023 full text (assent 12 June 2023) -> ndpc.gov.ng/news/ (Aug 2026 enforcement items). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior desk pass: prior cited '1,368 compliance notices (NDPC; Jones Day Aug 2025)' - that figure could not be found in any NDPC publication checked (Annual Reports 2024, 2025; GAID; news). NDPC's own counters (above) are used instead. Presence and operation are unambiguous; the GAID effective date (19 Sept 2025) rests on T4 legal analyses since the GAID text's transition clause references NDPA s.64 without naming the date.
cells.protocol_issues: None material. Law-firm client alerts (Jones Day) sit awkwardly between T4 and T5; recommend the defect log treat them as corroboration-only.

cells.source_title: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 (5th edition), Nigeria country profile, report p.45
cells.search_trail: ITU DataHub datahub.itu.int (403 to WebFetch/curl; browser attempt aborted - shared pane contention) -> ITU GCI landing page -> GCI 2024 report PDF downloaded from itu.int; tier lists (Tier 3 'Establishing', score 55-85, lists Nigeria, report pp.24-25) and Nigeria country profile page 45 read visually (pillar scores rendered as graphics, not extractable text). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: The GCIv5 report publishes per-country PILLAR scores but no overall score. Nigeria (profile p.45): Legal 19.52, Technical 18.88, Organizational 16.57, Capacity Development 13.15, Cooperation 14.28 (each /20) - sum 82.40/100 = 0.824 normalized, matching the 82.40 widely reported from ITU DataHub. Tier: T3 'Establishing' (55-85 band). SINGLE-SOURCE flag: the exact overall figure rests on one T1 document (by pillar summation); press corroboration (Nairametrics/Guardian, Sept 2024) is T5 and noted here only. Prior's caution stands: ITU places Nigeria in Tier 3 although 0.824 crosses the 0.8 threshold rung - tiers are ITU's own peer-grouping (T1 = 95-100), not the DAMM threshold.
cells.protocol_issues: 1) Indicator is defined on a 0-1 overall score that ITU no longer publishes directly in the report; value derived by summing the five published pillar scores (arithmetic identity under GCI methodology, 20 pts/pillar). 2) ITU DataHub, the only source naming 82.4 as a single number, is unreachable programmatically (403). 3) DAMM threshold H 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8 diverges from ITU's own tier bands - worth a spec note.

cells.notes: 2024 edition (latest publishing an overall score): Nigeria Total 43.33/100 (Government 59.88, Technology Sector 27.11, Data & Infrastructure 42.99). 2025 edition (Jan 2026 version, supersedes Dec 2025 release): Nigeria ranks 70/195 with pillar scores Policy Capacity 80.50, AI Infrastructure 39.10, Governance 78.13, Public Sector Adoption 47.46, Development & Diffusion 39.45, AI Resilience 42.66; top-4 in Sub-Saharan Africa behind South Africa (65), Mauritius (67), Kenya (68). FILLS prior desk-pass gap (4.3 was DATA GAP). Single-source by nature (proprietary index); FMCIDE's own statement cites '72nd', the rank in the superseded Dec 2025 release.
cells.protocol_issues: 1) The 2025 edition restructured pillars and dropped the published overall score, so the indicator as defined (0-100, threshold H 20/40/60/80) is only scoreable on the 2024 edition - vintage vs definition tension; ledger should route for refresh when Oxford Insights publishes 2025/2026 score data. 2) Rank moved 72 -> 70 between the Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 versions of the same edition; cite the January version only.

cells.value: No adopted national digital agriculture strategy as of Aug 2026. The Nigeria Digital Agriculture Strategy (NDAS) 2020-2030 remains a DRAFT (Nov 2020) on NITDA's site, still framed as open for stakeholder input. The operative policy anchors are NATIP 2022-2027 and the new National Agri-food Systems Investment Plan (NASIP, March 2026), which references NATIP throughout and never mentions NDAS.
cells.quality_evidence: None for adoption: no gazetting, ownership, budget line or implementation structure attaches to NDAS. Digital-agriculture delivery instead proceeds programmatically: NASIP includes digital-technology adoption and a performance-based digital extension system among its programs; FMAFS launched a National Digital Farmers Registry stakeholder process under the FG-IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan (20 Nov 2025) and a National Cooperative Smart Registry / cooperative digital-identity MoU (Aug 2026).
cells.source_title: NITDA - Draft National Digital Agriculture Strategy (NDAS) page + draft PDF (Nov 2020)
cells.search_trail: NITDA NDAS page (status: draft, workshop-for-inputs framing) -> NDAS draft PDF (title page: 'DRAFT... NOVEMBER, 2020') -> NASIP 2026 full text on agriculture.gov.ng (grep: zero NDAS mentions; NATIP is the anchor policy) -> agriculture.gov.ng site search 'digital' (registry launch Nov 2025, cooperative digitalization Aug 2026; no strategy adoption) -> fmcide.gov.ng site search 'agriculture' (AI Scaling Hub only). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: CONFIRMS prior desk pass (Announced 2020, never adopted, stale). 2025-26 check requested by guidance found no adoption event; what is new is programmatic: FG-IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan (T3 mention in FMAFS release, 20 Nov 2025) and cooperative-sector digital registries (Aug 2026). NATIP 2022-2027 official text also mirrored at uploads.cnfa.org (T4 host). Year recorded as 2026 = status observation date; the draft artefact itself is 2020 (stale).
cells.protocol_issues: Ladder ambiguity: a 6-year-old unadopted draft plus active digital-ag programs without a strategy - 'Announced' fits the strategy object, but the rung understates programmatic activity; assessor should read notes.

cells.value: Absent - refutation attempted and failed. No agricultural data governance framework (sector rules on agricultural data sharing, ownership, or access) was found in force. NASIP 2026 (the sector's flagship plan) contains no agricultural-data-governance provisions; the general-purpose NDPA 2023/GAID 2025 regime contains no agriculture-specific framework; the only instrument that gestures at ag-data arrangements (draft NDAS 2020: 'Data as a Service/Data Market', open agricultural data initiatives) was never adopted.
cells.source_title: National Agri-food Systems Investment Plan (NASIP) 2026, FMAFS - full text checked (negative finding)
cells.search_trail: NASIP 2026 full text (grep 'agricultural data / data shar / open data / data polic': zero hits) -> NDAS 2020 draft full text (open-data and DaaS aspirations only, unadopted) -> NDPC GAID 2025 full text (general regime, no sectoral ag framework) -> NAIS Sept 2025 (no ag-data governance) -> agriculture.gov.ng site search (National Digital Farmers Registry workshop invokes NDPA/ONSA safeguards, not a sector framework) -> nimc.gov.ng FMAFS/NIMC farmer-registry release (NIN-linkage architecture, no data-governance framework). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: CONFIRMS prior 'Absent' (prior was assessor judgement; this pass grounds it in named negative checks across the current flagship documents). Closest adjacent facts: the NIN-enabled farmer registry links farmer biometric identity to farmland and crop/livestock data under presidential NIN-use circular (NIMC release, Jan 2025), and the registry workshop names ONSA for data-protection safeguards - governance by general instruments, not an agricultural data framework. AGI prerequisite remains unmet.
cells.protocol_issues: Proving absence: trail lists the specific artefacts checked; a FAOLEX sweep was not possible after the session's search budget was exhausted - flag for loop 2.

cells.value: Final National Artificial Intelligence Strategy published September 2025 (81 pp, FMCIDE, hosted on NCAIR/NITDA official site, dated 19-09-2025, no draft watermark; the August 2024 predecessor was watermarked DRAFT). Agriculture is a named priority application sector - lighthouse projects across 'vital economic sectors (e.g., agriculture, healthcare, education, finance)' (§3.1.1), sector-specific AI adoption roadmaps (§3.1.2), and economic-productivity objectives - but there is no dedicated agriculture chapter or pillar (the five pillars are functional).
cells.quality_evidence: Implementation vehicles exist: Nigeria AI Scaling Hub launched 3 June 2025 with the Gates Foundation (up to USD 7.5m over three years) explicitly to scale AI in health, agriculture and education (FMCIDE release); NCAIR is the institutional home; 3MTT trains AI/ML talent at scale. Oxford Insights 2025 credits Nigeria with 'a detailed roadmap including both long and shorter-term goals'. Formal FEC-approval language does not appear in the strategy document itself.
cells.search_trail: NCAIR (ncair.nitda.gov.ng) homepage -> NAIS Sept 2025 PDF full text (foreword, pillar structure, agriculture mentions at 12+ loci) -> NAIS Aug 2024 PDF (DRAFT watermark confirmed) -> FMCIDE AI Scaling Hub release (3 June 2025; minister: strategy drafting 'recently' completed) -> FMCIDE Jan 2026 statement (AI literacy, GAIRI rank) -> Oxford Insights 2025 report SSA section. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior: prior recorded 'NAIS 2024 adopted'. Corrected chronology: Aug 2024 = draft (watermarked); June 2025 = drafting completed per minister; 19 Sept 2025 = final version published on official infrastructure. 'Adopted' rung rests on official publication of the final strategy by the responsible ministry; no FEC gazette/approval instrument was found - if the ladder requires formal executive adoption, treat as at the Announced/Adopted boundary.
cells.protocol_issues: Adoption evidence standard for strategies (official publication vs formal executive approval) is undefined in the indicator guidance - recurring issue across 4.4/4.6; needs a spec ruling.

cells.value: NIN coverage ~49-57% of total population as of 30 June 2026: 117,493,554 persons issued a NIN, out of 134,553,120 NINs enrolled (World Bank ISR, Nigeria Digital Identification for Development P167183, 11 Aug 2026), against WDI total population 237,527,782 (2025) -> 49.5% (persons issued) to 56.6% (NINs enrolled). Baseline 36.9m (Oct 2019); project target 180m by Dec 2026, with a stated gap of 62.5m and current run-rate 1.5-1.8m/month.
cells.source_title: World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report, Nigeria Digital Identification for Development (P167183), 11 Aug 2026
cells.search_trail: nimc.gov.ng enrolment-report and enrolment-dashboard (JS-only, no citable figures) -> NIMC press-release/speeches APIs scanned in full (latest official total on NIMC's own site: 'over 109 million NINs issued', CRV Day statement 13 Aug 2024) -> World Bank documents API (search.worldbank.org/api/v3/wds) -> latest ISR P167183 (Aug 2026) full text, results indicators extracted -> WDI SP.POP.TOTL via api.worldbank.org (2025: 237,527,782). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE from prior (57.2% = '137.4M NIN Jul 2026 / ~240M pop'): the July 2026 '136m+ enrolments' milestone exists only in press (T5 - inadmissible) and could not be found on NIMC's own site; the verified June 2026 ISR numbers distinguish NINs ENROLLED (134.6m - close to the press figure) from persons ISSUED (117.5m). Coverage is 40-60 threshold band under every defensible numerator/denominator combination, so the prior's band survives although its point value does not. Ward-Level Enrollment Drive and NIMC Act 2026 (single-ID policy) underway. Percentages are derived (numerator WB ISR/NIMC admin data; denominator WDI) - both components named by their sources.
cells.protocol_issues: 1) Indicator wants '% adults or population' - adult-share is unpublished; population basis used and labeled. 2) World Bank ISRs are official IO project reporting but task-team self-reported: per the protocol's open judgement call on donor project reports, tiered T4 here, not T2 - Katreyna to rule. 3) NIMC publishes no current machine-readable enrolment total; its dashboard is uncitable - structural refresh risk for this cell.

cells.value: No standing inter-ministerial body coordinating digital agriculture (FMAFS + FMCIDE/NITDA) found - refutation attempted. Coordination is project-based and multiplying: FMAFS-NIMC NIN-enabled Farmer Registry & G2P Card project (Jan 2025); a Multi-Stakeholder Knowledge-Sharing Platform inaugurated at the National Digital Farmers Registry workshop (20 Nov 2025; FMAFS with NIMC, ONSA, IFAD under the FG-IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan); the FMCIDE-led AI Scaling Hub (June 2025) with agriculture in scope. Sector-wide governance (NASIP/NATIP: National Implementation Committee, Technical Working Committee, NCAFS, Agriculture Sector Working Group) coordinates agriculture MDAs generally - the ICT ministry is not a named member and digital agriculture has no dedicated organ.
cells.quality_evidence: NASIP 2026 institutionalises quarterly inter-ministerial meetings and a Community of Practice among agriculture-sector MDAs (budgeted in the NATIP implementation matrix) and names inter-ministerial coordination among the sector's acknowledged weaknesses; none of this is digital-agriculture-specific or ag+ICT bilateral.
cells.source_title: FMAFS - Nigeria launches National Digital Farmers Registry (workshop + Multi-Stakeholder Knowledge-Sharing Platform), 20 Nov 2025
cells.search_trail: NASIP 2026 governance chapter full read (committees/TWGs, stakeholder roles - no ICT-ministry membership, no digital-ag organ) -> agriculture.gov.ng site search 'digital' (registry, cooperative digitalization) -> FMAFS registry release (platform inauguration, agency roster) -> NIMC press API (FMAFS/NIMC project detail) -> fmcide.gov.ng site search 'agriculture' (AI Scaling Hub only; no joint committee with FMAFS) -> NDAS draft (its proposed governance structure was never stood up). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.notes: CONFIRMS prior ('no standing mechanism; coordination project-based') with updated 2025-26 facts: the Nov 2025 Knowledge-Sharing Platform is the closest thing to a standing coordination venue but is registry-scoped and multi-stakeholder rather than an inter-ministerial digital-ag committee. DELIVERY flag remains warranted: every observed mechanism is tied to a single project/programme lifecycle.
cells.protocol_issues: Ladder ambiguity: the indicator object is a 'standing body/committee'; operating project-level platforms do not clear that bar but are more than nothing - rung semantics (Absent vs Announced) need a spec ruling for partial/project-based coordination.

bundle_issues: 1) The session's WebSearch budget (200 calls, shared across the gauntlet's parallel bundles) was exhausted early in this bundle's run; all verification after the first four searches was done via WebFetch, curl, and official APIs on known URLs. Corroboration sweeps (FAOLEX for 4.5, additional second sources for 4.2/4.3) were cut short - flag for loop 2. 2) The shared browser pane is contended by other concurrent gauntlet sessions (tabs were navigated out from under this session twice); browser-based verification of JS-only sources (ITU DataHub, NIMC enrolment dashboard) had to be abandoned - two key T1/T3 dashboards are effectively unreachable to programmatic assessors. 3) Systemic source shifts worth a spec note: ITU GCIv5 no longer publishes overall country scores (tiers + pillar scores only; overall must be derived by summation), and Oxford Insights 2025 dropped the published overall 0-100 score entirely - both C3 threshold indicators (4.2, 4.3) now sit on derived or prior-edition values. 4) The prior desk pass contained two material errors corrected here: 'NAIS 2024 adopted' (final NAIS is Sept 2025; the 2024 document is a watermarked draft) and digital-ID 57.2% built on a T5 press figure (verified WB ISR June 2026 gives 117.5m issued / 134.6m enrolled -> 49-57% band-consistent). Its 4.1 enforcement statistic (1,368 compliance notices) could not be reproduced from NDPC's own publications. 5) Access date for every citation: 2026-08-22.
